sections.h2: Why does each industry need a different GEO approach?
sections.html:
Generative engine optimisation (GEO, spelt optimization in the US) works the same way everywhere at the level of method: find the questions, see who the engines name, trace which sources they quote, fix those sources and measure again. What changes by industry is everything inside that method.

  • The questions differ. A homebuyer asks about possession dates. An investor asks about the last quarter. A procurement engineer asks about a material grade.
  • The sources differ. Engines lean on property portals for flats, exchange filings for listed companies, review sites for software and medical references for medicines.
  • The rules differ. RERA, SEBI, FSSAI, the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, professional body codes and CBFC certification all limit what a brand may say, and so what we may publish for it.

That is why we start every programme with a Week-1 baseline built from your own category, not a template.

sections.h2: Which sources do AI engines lean on in real estate?
sections.html:
Our Sources view records every citation behind every answer. In real estate and hospitality the same groups come up again and again:

  • Property portals: project listings, configurations and buyer reviews.
  • State RERA websites: registration numbers, carpet areas, possession timelines and complaints.
  • Google Business Profiles and reviews for project sites, sales offices and hotels.
  • News and property media: launches, delays and disputes.
  • YouTube site walkthroughs and vlogs, especially when they carry full transcripts.
  • Reddit and city forums: home-buying threads for Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai and other cities.
  • Travel review sites, booking platforms and travel blogs for hotels and resorts.
  • Wikipedia and Wikidata for larger developers and hotel groups.

sections.h2: What usually goes wrong in AI answers for real estate?
sections.html:
• Old possession dates or configurations copied from stale portal listings.
  • A project confused with a similarly named project, or placed in the wrong micro-market.
  • A resolved complaint or an old delay still leading the answer.
  • A competitor named first because its listings and reviews are more complete.
  • New launches missing entirely because no source the engines trust mentions them yet.
  • Hotel answers built on a handful of old reviews.

sections.h2: Which sources do AI engines lean on in financial services?

  • Rates, fees or product features quoted from old pages.
  • A creator's opinion presented as the company's own position.
  • The brand missing from "best X" shortlists because comparison sites carry stale data.

sections.h2: Which rules do we work inside in financial services?
sections.html:
• SEBI: public disclosures only, nothing unpublished or price-sensitive, nothing ahead of an exchange filing, and no forward-looking promises.
  • Who may advise: we stay inside SEBI's limits on investment advice and on tie-ups with unregistered finance creators.
  • RBI and IRDAI expectations for regulated lenders and insurers, including required disclosures and risk statements.
  • ASCI: no assured returns and no claims without evidence.
  • DPDP Act: lead and chat data handled with consent.

The company signs off every change before it is published.
